subject: Re: is there a way to set data as cluster sizes in an existing

messages.author: f0732d7bffc290cf
messages.subject: is there a way to set data as cluster sizes in an existing
parts:
Hi All,
I am currently analysing a large multi-species data set in DISTANCE 6.
I have tackled the analysis of many species by setting up several
hundred different analyses based on filters which select only a single
species at a time, which I then use as input into various model
combinations for analysis. unfortunately I have only recently thought
to re-incorporate cluster size information into my data set, which i had
omitted earlier due to the complexity it added (but I now see it is
necessary to include it, as some species do occur in clusters). Though
I have imported the data with a cluster size variable added and each
observation entry collapsed into its cluster, Distance does not seem to
recognise the cluster info, and cluster size estimates to not appear in
my analysis outputs. There is an option to select data as cluster sizes
in the project set-up menu, but I want to avoid setting up my several
hundred analyses again if possible, which will be necessary if I have to
start from scratch... is there a way to set data as cluster sizes in an
existing project? Any thoughts would be appreciated,
Cheers
Alex

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: is there a way to set data as cluster sizes in an existing
parts:
Alex:

I'm not certain that this will work, nor am I certain of the meaning of
your statement:
"Though I have imported the data with a cluster size variable added and
each observation entry collapsed into its cluster"

But you might try the following:

Go to the Surveys tab for your project, click on "New Survey" (which
ought to be the only survey in this project). Check that 'Survey
Methods and Data' show Observations to be 'Single objects.' Click on the
Properties button to change "Observations" from 'Single objects' to
'Clusters.'

Change Observations to 'Clusters of object' with the radio button in the
Survey Properties window and click OK. Move to the Data fields tab in
that same window, click upon the 'Field name' box adjacent to the
'Cluster size' row to indicate the name of the field in your project
that contains the information about the number of individuals in each
cluster.

That *may* get Distance to recognise the cluster size information
contained within your data.
